title: Coding agents: a hook, the gateway, the agent's own answer
lede: Each agent is covered through its own hook interface in the machine-level managed configuration. The decision returns in the agent's native shape. Ping release claim, UNVERIFIED on our tenant. Simulated.

nodes.label: Same policies and detection as LLM and MCP traffic
Audit trail: who, what, which laptop

edges.label: event + identity and device from the certificate
prompt, command, file read, MCP call, tool result
the agent's native allow, deny or ask

steps.title: The agent fires its hook
steps.what: Before a prompt is sent, a shell command runs, a file is read or an MCP tool is called (and after a tool returns), the agent writes the event as JSON to the hook's stdin. The hook is in the machine-level managed configuration, so the developer installed nothing.

steps.title: The hook asks the gateway
steps.what: The hook posts the event with the developer's identity and the device, taken from the machine's certificate. If the gateway cannot be reached the hook follows its failure policy: keep working and record the gap, or refuse when the tenant set FailClosed.

steps.title: The same detection runs
steps.what: Secrets, shell metacharacters and destructive commands, sensitive paths, unapproved MCP servers and hidden instructions are evaluated by the same gateway, policies and detection as LLM and MCP traffic.

steps.title: A decision comes back
steps.what: Deny for a credential in a prompt, ask for a sensitive read, alert for a risky argument that should not interrupt local work, allow otherwise.

steps.title: It is recorded
steps.what: One audit trail across every surface: who ran what on which laptop, with prompt text redacted.

steps.title: The decision goes back to the hook
The agent answers in its own language
steps.what: The hook prints that agent's native allow, deny or ask, so a refusal appears in the developer's normal permission dialog with the reason, not as an error.
